title: Ribosome preparation from turquoise killifish skeletal muscle for cryo-EM
protocol: Transfer fish (5–6 weeks after hatching) to 1.5 g/L tricaine methanosulfate solution until gill movement stops completely.
Remove skin by cutting along yellow lines shown in Figure 1.
Collect skeletal muscle area indicated by the black line in Figure 1, avoiding contamination with other tissues.
Freeze collected muscle tissue in liquid nitrogen.
Store frozen muscle tissue at -80°C before use.
Grind the frozen muscle finely (particle size < 100 μm) using a mortar and pestle in liquid nitrogen.
Grind 600 mg of skeletal muscle for 15 min on ice until the powder sticks tightly to the mortar wall even in the presence of liquid nitrogen.
Add 200 mg aliquots of ground tissue powder to e-tubes.
Store the tubes at -80°C.
Homogenize 600 mg of finely ground skeletal muscle in 30 mL of homogenization buffer on ice.
Filter the homogenized tissue through two layers of miracloth.
Transfer the filtered homogenate to a polypropylene centrifuge tube.
Prepare sucrose cushion buffer by filling an ultra-clear centrifuge tube from the bottom using a long-tip Pasteur pipette without forming bubbles.
Load the protein extract onto the prepared sucrose cushion.
Centrifuge at 14,000×g for 5 min at 4°C to remove debris.
Transfer supernatant into polypropylene centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 30,000×g for 20 min at 4°C.
Collect clear supernatant in a 50 mL tube.
Prepare sucrose cushion tubes by adding 4 mL of sucrose cushion buffer to ultra-clear centrifuge tubes.
Load cleared solution onto sucrose cushion.
Heat-seal the top of the tube after balancing.
Centrifuge at 150,000×g for 12 h at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant very carefully so as not to lose the ribosome pellet.
Very carefully wash the pellets three times with 1 mL of washing buffer.
Make sure the ribosome pellet stays on the tube wall during each wash.
Check for a transparent ribosome pellet at the bottom of the tube.
Collect the ribosome pellets with a tip and resuspend them in 50 μL of resuspension buffer.
Cut the pipette tip diagonally to aid in collecting the ribosome pellet from the e-tube wall.
Add resuspension buffer directly to the centrifuge tube to collect remaining ribosome pellets.
Gently dissolve ribosome pellets by pipetting without forming bubbles.
Centrifuge at 20,000×g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer the clear supernatant to a new tube.
Measure optical density (OD) at 260 nm to check ribosome purity.
Glow discharge a grid (Quantifoil R2/2) with argon gas for 30 sec.
Load 4 μl of isolated ribosome onto the grid and incubate for 30 sec.
Wash the grid twice by placing the grid briefly onto a drop of distilled water.
Remove excess water from the grid by touching the grid edge with filter paper.
Incubate the grid in uranyl acetate for 30 sec.
Wash the grid twice by placing the grid briefly onto a drop of distilled water.
Remove excess water from the grid by touching the grid edge with filter paper.
Dry the grid for 5 min at 25°C.
Glow discharge both sides of a new grid with argon gas for 30 seconds.
Coat the grid with graphene oxide.
Load 3 μL of graphene oxide solution onto the carbon side and incubate for 2 minutes.
Remove excess graphene oxide from the grid by touching the edge to filter paper.
Wash the grid three times in distilled water drops.
Dry the grid for 5 minutes.
Store grids in liquid nitrogen before imaging and data collection.
Collect data.
